beat_player.text: Good field work, {player}. You kept your line when it mattered. Most would have broken at the ford.
You paid {troop_count} men for that hill, {player}. Come by after and I'll show you where you could have saved half.
{player}, you won this one. Enjoy it while the {gold} lasts. It does not buy a second chance at Castelnarc.
Charging downhill with {troop_count} men was never going to end well. I have the notebook to prove it.

beat_by_player.text: Well played, {player}. Hard to hold a line like that with only {troop_count} men. Good eye for the ground.
You had me on the flank, {player}. Come by after and I will walk you through where my {troop_count} went wrong.
Hm, {player}. You beat me today. In the first war I'd have lost the whole column that way. Still, the notebook keeps a count.
{player} won the day, and I lost {troop_count} men to a bad scout report. Note it, newcomers. Don't trust the scouts.

fought_alongside_player.text: Good work with {player} today. {troop_count} men and not one reckless charge. That is how the fens were held, back in the first war.
That was clean, {player}. We broke {enemy_faction} because nobody ran ahead of the line. Buy the next round when we're back :)
{player}, you kept your place in the line. Good. Plenty of people forget that wars are won in the boring parts.
{enemy_faction} will remember that field for a while. Shared victories are the only kind I trust these days.

released_by_player.text: You let me walk instead of taking the ransom, {player}. I won't forget that. The next siege I run, you get the first seat.
{player} released me without ransom. Rare enough to mention. Ransom makes for tidier books, but mercy keeps the roads open.
Letting me go cost you a good ransom, {player}. Don't make a habit of it or the others will start expecting the same.
Gracious of {player} to let me walk. Most would have squeezed the purse. Remember that when your own turn comes.

player_joined_my_faction.text: {player} has sworn to {my_faction}. Welcome. Keep your head down for the first month and listen more than you talk.
So you've come to {my_faction}, {player}. Good. Read the old charters before you argue with anyone, they save a lot of grief.
{player}, {my_faction} is a long road for a man who has only just arrived. Prove the oath was not a convenience.
Be kind to the new ones, that's my rule. {player} will learn {my_faction} the slow way, like the rest of us.

player_granted_fief.text: {fief} to {player}. Well earned, I think. The last holder lost it by being too eager. Learn from that.
You have {fief} now, {player}. I've held worse, and I've lost better. Keep the walls manned and the granary full.
{fief} went to {player}. I will not say the choice was wrong. I will say I kept my notes on the last three who held it.
Hm. {player} got {fief}. Let us see how long the walls stand before we start clapping.

encounter_greeting.text: Ah, {player}. {persona} of {my_faction}, at your service. Sit by the fire a moment, the road ahead is muddy and I have tea.
{player}. {persona}, {my_faction}. Your party is on the wrong side of the ridge, you know. Let me show you the way round.
{player}. We meet again on the map. Keep to your side of the river and we both get home for dinner.
Well met, {player}. {persona} here. Heard you were in the fens last season. Tell me it wasn't as bad as the rumors.

encounter_farewell.text: Safe road, {player}. Mind the bridge at the crossing, it has been sagging since the first war and nobody has fixed it.
That will do for now, {player}. We will meet again on the map. I'll be the one with a notebook.
Go on then, {player}. Keep your banners out of my fields and we shall have no trouble.
Until the next ridge, {player}. Eat something hot before you march, and keep your men dry.

ambient_chatter.text: Rain on the road to {town} again. Anyone who says the fens have dried out has never walked them in autumn.
The granary in {village} is half empty this season. Bring grain before the price climbs and you'll thank yourself.
Notes for newcomers: a siege lasts longer than the first hour looks like it will. Plan supplies for three months.
Heard the bridge at {town} finally got repaired. Took a decade. We are a patient folk here.

player_big_defeat.text: Hard day, {player}. Losing {troop_count} men in one go happens to all of us. I lost a column at Castelnarc once.
I saw the field, {player}. A bad morning, not a finished campaign. Come by and I'll show you the notebook.
{player} lost most of the army near the ford. Scouts first, banners second, that's the old lesson. Write it down.
{troop_count} men gone, {player}. I told you the ridge was a trap. Rebuild and do not wave your banner so loudly next time.
